## Event probabilities and Venn diagrams

### Newspaper readership

*2022/2023 · Q1 · p. 2*

Of 50 people surveyed, 25 read newspaper $A$, 16 read $B$, and 14 read $C$. Five read both $A$ and $B$, four read both $B$ and $C$, six read both $C$ and $A$, and two read all three.

a. Sketch a Venn diagram showing these data. (1 mark)
b. For a person chosen at random from the group, find the probability that they read

    i. at least one of the newspapers (2 marks),
    ii. exactly one of the newspapers (2 marks),
    iii. only newspaper $A$ (1 mark).

### Cinema and premiere tickets

*2025/2026 · Part B, Q1 · p. 4*

In a survey, 15% of participants had never bought either kind of ticket, 73% had bought cinema tickets, and 49% had never bought premiere tickets.

a. For a participant chosen at random, find the probability that they had bought

    i. cinema tickets or premiere tickets (3 marks),
    ii. both cinema tickets and premiere tickets (4 marks),
    iii. cinema tickets only (3 marks).

b. Sketch a Venn diagram and label each region with its percentage. (3 marks)

## Continuous random variables and expectation

### Moments of a continuous random variable

*2022/2023 · Q2 · p. 2*

The continuous random variable $X$ has density $f(x)=(x+3)/20$ for $0\leq x\leq 4$. Compute each expectation.

a. $E(X)$ (3 marks)
b. $E(2X+5)$ (2 marks)
c. $E(X^2)$ (3 marks)
d. $E(X^2+2X-3)$ (2 marks)

\newpage

## Discrete distributions and binomial probabilities

### Weekly magazine sales

*2025/2026 · Part B, Q2 · pp. 4–5*

A sales agent stocks 12 magazines each week and has regular orders for 9. The number of additional copies sold varies. Past sales give the following estimated probabilities.

| Copies sold | 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 |
|:------------|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Probability | 0.20 | 0.35 | 0.30 | 0.15 |

a. Estimate the mean number of copies sold per week. (3 marks)
b. The agent pays 85 cents per copy and sells each copy for RM1.45. Unsold copies are destroyed. Calculate the profit in a week when 11 copies are sold. (2 marks)

### Distribution of a binomial count

*2022/2023 · Q3 · p. 2*

Let $Y\sim\operatorname{Bin}(4,0.8)$.

a. Construct the probability distribution of $Y$ and compute its expectation and variance. (8 marks)
b. Show that $E(Y)=np$ and $\operatorname{Var}(Y)=npq$, where $q=1-p$. (2 marks)

### Frozen pie deliveries

*2025/2026 · Part B, Q5 · p. 5 · 6 marks*

Three percent of the frozen pies delivered to a canteen are contaminated. On a morning when 500 pies are delivered, find the probability that 15 or more are contaminated.

## Normal probabilities

### Areas under the standard normal curve

*2025/2026 · Part A, Q1 · p. 2 · 20 marks*

For a standard normal random variable $Z$, compute each probability.

a. $P(-0.25 < Z < 0.25)$
b. $P(0.00 < Z < 0.65)$
c. $P(-1.90 < Z < 0.04)$
d. $P(-0.49 < Z < 0.55)$
e. $P\!\left(\dfrac{65-60}{\sqrt{625}} < Z < \dfrac{87-60}{\sqrt{625}}\right)$

### Masses of packets

*2022/2023 · Q4 · p. 3*

Packet masses are normally distributed with mean 1.42 kg and standard deviation 0.025 kg.

a. Find the probability that a randomly selected packet weighs between 1.37 kg and 1.45 kg. (5 marks)
b. In a batch of 5,000 packets, how many would you expect to weigh less than 1.35 kg? (5 marks)

\newpage

## Sampling distributions of the mean

### Samples from a normal population

*2025/2026 · Part A, Q4 · p. 2 · 4 marks*

A random sample $X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_{28}$ is drawn from $N(193,225)$, where 225 is the population variance. Compute $P(\bar X>200)$.

### Students’ interest in online games

*2025/2026 · Part A, Q3 · p. 2 · 5 marks*

A researcher studying students’ interest in types of online games takes a random sample of 36 from a normal population with mean $\mu=155$ and variance $\sigma^2=125$. Find the probability that the sample mean exceeds 157.

### Sample means for count data

*2022/2023 · Q5 · p. 3*

Thirty random observations are taken from each of the following distributions. In each case, find the probability that the sample mean exceeds 5.

a. $Y$ counts the telephone calls made to a counselling service in one evening, with $Y\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(4.5)$. (4 marks)
b. $Y$ counts the heads obtained in nine tosses of a fair coin. (6 marks)

## Estimation and confidence intervals

### A population proportion

*2025/2026 · Part B, Q3 · p. 5*

In a random sample of 200 students, 150 drove to college alone.

a. Calculate the sample proportion who drove to college alone. (2 marks)
b. Construct a 90% confidence interval for the population proportion who drove to college alone. (8 marks)

### Mean and variance from height measurements

*2022/2023 · Q6 · p. 3*

Researchers measured the heights $x$, in centimetres, of a random sample of 200 men living in Malaysia. They obtained $\sum x=35{,}050$ and $\sum x^2=6{,}163{,}109$.

a. Compute unbiased estimates of the population mean and variance of height. (4 marks)
b. Construct an approximate 90% confidence interval for the population mean height. (5 marks)

### Recovering information from a confidence interval

*2025/2026 · Part B, Q4 · p. 5*

Men’s heights in a district have mean $\mu$ cm and standard deviation $\sigma$ cm. A random sample of 100 men gave a 95% confidence interval of $(177.22,197.18)$ cm for $\mu$.

a. Calculate the sample mean. (6 marks)
b. Calculate $\sigma$. (2 marks)
c. Calculate a 90% confidence interval for $\mu$. (6 marks)

\newpage

## Hypothesis tests for a population mean

### Critical values of Student’s $t$

*2025/2026 · Part A, Q2 · p. 2 · 6 marks*

Find the critical $t$-value or values for each test.

a. A left-tailed test with $\alpha=0.05$ and sample size $n=23$.
b. A two-tailed test with $\alpha=0.01$ and 17 degrees of freedom.
c. A two-tailed test with $\alpha=0.02$ and 7 degrees of freedom.
d. A right-tailed test with $\alpha=0.1$ and sample size $n=5$.

### A two-tailed $Z$-test

*2025/2026 · Part A, Q5 · p. 3 · 8 marks*

Give the five steps for conducting a two-tailed $Z$-test for a population mean at $\alpha=0.05$.

### Statistics exam scores

*2025/2026 · Part B, Q6 · p. 6 · 9 marks*

All IT students at UMT took a statistics exam. A random sample of their scores gave the following results.

| Sample variance $S^2$ | Sample size $n$ | Sample mean $\bar X$ |
|----------------------:|----------------:|--------------------:|
| 55 | 15 | 40 |

Use a $t$-test at the 5% significance level to test whether the population mean score equals 45.

## Chi-square goodness of fit

### A binomial model for heifer calves

*2022/2023 · Q7 · p. 4*

A farmer recorded the number of heifer calves born to each cow during its first years of breeding.

| Number of heifers | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|:------------------|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Number of cows | 4 | 19 | 41 | 52 | 26 | 8 |

a. At the 5% significance level, test whether a binomial distribution with $n=5$ and $p=0.5$ adequately models these data. (10 marks)
b. If $n$ stays fixed at 5 and you estimate $p$ from the data, how does the test change? (5 marks)
